summary: Elevator codes are concatenated classical codes designed for biased-noise qubits, combining inner repetition phase-flip codes ($d_Z^\mathrm{inner}$ variable, $d_X^\mathrm{inner}=1$) with high-rate outer bit-flip codes executed at the logical level. For noise bias $\eta \geq 7\times10^4$, these codes reduce qubit overhead by over 50% compared to rectangular and XZZX surface codes at $p_Z=10^{-3}$ and $\eta=2\times10^6$ when achieving logical error rate $10^{-12}$.
motivation: Biased-noise qubits like superconducting cat qubits exhibit exponential bit-flip suppression at the cost of increased phase-flip errors, but existing asymmetric codes either suffer from low thresholds (rectangular surface code) or require twice as many qubits (XZZX code) to maintain code distance. The authors exploit concatenation to address phase-flip and bit-flip errors at different layers for better resource efficiency in the strong-bias regime.
method: Inner codes are phase-flip repetition codes supporting transversal CNOTs; outer codes are matchable classical linear codes ($[15,9,3]$, $[15,6,5]$, $[16,3,8]$) designed to correct only bit-flip errors ($d_Z^\mathrm{outer}=1$) to avoid logical hook errors. Outer code syndrome extraction uses sequential transversal CNOT and SWAP gates between stacked inner code blocks, decoded with BP+OSD to handle hypergraph structure. Overall code achieves $d_X = d_X^\mathrm{inner} \cdot d_X^\mathrm{outer}$ and $d_Z = d_Z^\mathrm{inner} \cdot d_Z^\mathrm{outer}$.
result: At $p_Z=10^{-3}$ and $\eta=10^6$, concatenated codes achieve $3\times$ lower overhead than XZZX and $2\times$ lower than thin surface codes for logical error $10^{-12}$; at $p_Z=10^{-2}$ and $\eta=10^6$, advantage reaches $3\times$ for errors $10^{-6}$–$10^{-11}$ due to phase-flip threshold roughly five times higher than surface code.
